thread:
maya: heads up — CI matrix started failing on the paged/fused-attn build when using the `python:3.11-slim` images. first failure showed up on gcc 13 variant.

ci-bot: build 1945678901-3 (paged-attn / gcc13 / slim) FAILED — linking error in fused_kernel.so (exit code 1). log: `ld: /workspace/build/fused_kernel.so: undefined reference to \`__atomic_fetch_add_8\'`

lucas: ugh, saw that locally too. looks like a missing -latomic or libstdc++ mismatch when toolchain != host. can you paste the exact link command?

maya: link cmd (trimmed):
```
/usr/bin/g++ -shared -o fused_kernel.so obj/*.o -Wl,--no-undefined -L/usr/local/lib -lstdc++ -lpthread
```
maya: also noticed `-fopenmp` is in CXXFLAGS on some runners, not others. intermittent symbol issues.

ravi: common culprit — slim images strip some dev libs. `python:3.11-slim` in our infra is missing libatomic by default on gcc13. adding `apt-get install -y libatomic1` fixes the undefined ref for me. but that doesn't feel like the real root cause.

jenny: how does this affect runtime? are we seeing segfaults in the paged-attn tests or just build failures?

maya: mostly build failures so far. but i ran the fused-attn microbench on the gcc13-slim built wheel and saw a ~8% perf regression vs the bookworm/gcc12 wheel. `perf record` shows fewer AVX512 vector instructions — looks like the compiler chose a more conservative codegen.

lucas: is that with `-O3 -march=native` or with portable flags? CI uses portable flags: `-O2 -march=x86-64-v2`. if images change glibc/libstdc++ version we might accidentally pick different inline asm paths in our kernels.

maya: exact build envs:
- failing: `python:3.11-slim` (gcc 13, libstdc++ 13.2)
- passing: `debian:bookworm-slim` (gcc 12, libstdc++ 12.1)

maya: sample failing log lines: 
```
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
/usr/bin/ld: fused_kernel.so: undefined reference to `__atomic_fetch_add_8'
/usr/bin/ld: fused_kernel.so: undefined reference to `__atomic_compare_exchange_16'
```

ravi: those are atomics for 8/16 byte ops; on some targets the compiler emits calls to libatomic. linking with `-latomic` or installing the proper libatomic package fixes it. but the perf regression suggests ABI/toolchain differences beyond just missing libs.

lucas: i repro'd perf regression: when building in slim container the compiler avoids `__builtin_ia32_xxx` intrinsics because of SSE/AVX detection differences. solution: ensure CMake explicitly sets `-march` target we expect for kernels (we currently let cmake/clang/gcc autodetect).

jenny: wouldn't setting `-march=native` in CI make wheels non-portable? we need manylinux-compatible artifacts.

lucas: yes. for CI we should build two artifact flavors: (1) portable manylinux wheel (no native march) for distribution, (2) optimized wheel (CI-only) for internal perf tests and bench comparisons. that way benchmarks are apples-to-apples.

maya: proposed immediate fixes:
1) in the slim build matrix job install `libatomic1` and `libstdc++6` explicit versions to match toolchain
2) force CMake flags for the fused/paged-attn subproject: `-DATTN_MARCH=x86-64-v3` (keeps portable but consistent)
3) add a perf-only CI job that builds with `-march=native` and runs the fused/paged benchmarks to detect regressions early

ci-bot: NOTE: job annotation: add matrix axis `CXX_FLAGS` (portable|native) — recommend conservative default portable.

ravi: one more weirdness: packaging step strips rpath in our wheel which means when runtime uses system libstdc++ it can pick older code paths. adding `auditwheel repair --plat manylinux_2_31_x86_64` preserved wheel and fixed runtime lookup in my local test.

lucas: good catch. we should also ensure compiled kernels embed `DT_RUNPATH` to the wheel's vendor libs (or vendor libstdc++). but that's more invasive. auditwheel + explicit `-latomic` should unblock CI right away.

maya: i'll open a small PR with: Dockerfile change (`apt-get install libatomic1`), cmake tweak to add `-DATTN_MARCH` default, and packaging change to run `auditwheel repair`. will also add a perf job to the build matrix.

jenny: thanks. can you add repro steps in the PR description? QA needs to run microbench after patch.

maya: will do. repro steps to include: 
```
# run slim build locally
docker run --rm -v $PWD:/w -w /w python:3.11-slim bash -lc "apt-get update && apt-get install -y build-essential libatomic1 && ./ci/build_wheel.sh"
# run benchmark
python -m microbench.fused --model tiny --runs 50
```

ravi: also add a tiny script to compare perf numbers with a golden baseline and fail CI if regress > 5%. avoids silent drift.

lucas: agreed. one caveat: flaky noise on small sample sizes. use median of 5 warmup + 20 runs.

maya: will implement. tagging @eng-sre for CI runner image changes and @eng-packaging for auditwheel steps. :thumbsup:

ci-bot: created issue #2224: "attn: CI matrix: slim image link failures + perf variance" and linked this thread.

jenny: great. once PR lands let's run the perf job across the last-good sha and current to see where we stand.

maya: thanks all — pushing PR shortly.
